To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gliclazide is effective in the treatment of NIDDM and is well tolerated.

the use of gliclazide in patients with NIDDM who are inadequately controlled on diet alone or oral agents is effective in reducing blood glucose, improving glycaemic control as measured by home‐monitoring, and reducing mean body weight, particularly in the obese and elderly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach to the design, synthesis and evaluation of new antidiabetic agents.
the study of the effects of gliclazide on blood glucose control and body weight in non‐insulin dependent diabetics.
the study of the effects of gliclazide on blood glucose control and body weight in non‐insulin dependent diabetics, using the home blood glucose monitoring technique, in a large multicentre trial.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

home blood glucose monitoring in non‐insulin diabetic patients is of great value in the management of their condition and the addition of gliclazide to their treatment improves their control of blood sugar.
home blood glucose monitoring is a valuable adjunct to the treatment of non‐insulin dependent diabetes.
the addition of gliclazide to the diet of a non‐insulin-dependent diabetic is a valuable method of improving blood glucose control and weight reduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gliclazide is a safe and effective hypoglycaemia‐inducing agent in NIDDM.
gliclazide is effective and well tolerated in the treatment of non‐insulin dependent diabetes.

the addition of gliclazide to a programme of home‐monitoring of glucose in patients with non‐insulin dependent diabetes mellitus improves blood glucose control and weight reduction, particularly in obese subjects and those previously treated with sulphonylures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a glucose meter can help patients to achieve better blood sugar control and that gliclazide is a useful drug for achieving this goal in non‐insulin diabetic patients.
home blood glucose monitoring is a useful tool for patients to monitor their own progress and to help them to adjust their medication and diet.
gliclazide, a second‐generation sulphonyurea, is effective in improving the glycaemic control of non‐insulin dependent diabetics, and is well tolerated by the majority of patients.
